hero.title:
Import your JDM to Spain.
Know the real cost.
hero.sub: Full cost calculator: EPA/MFN tariffs, VAT, individual or historic homologation, ITV, registration tax and DGT fees. Database of over 8,000 Japanese models.

process.sectionDesc: From the Japanese auction to Spanish plates. A summary of the main steps.
process.step1Desc: USS, TAA, JAA, HAA or AUCNET networks. Obtain an invoice with the VIN, the shakken (車検証) and all technical documentation for any modifications.
process.step2Desc: Deregister in Japan (yushutsu massho) and obtain the export certificate (yushutsu shōmeisho). Apostille the documents and ship the container to Spain.
process.step3Desc: Submit DUA, pay tariff (0% with EPA documentation, 10% MFN without) and VAT (21%). Obtain Certificate H1. Sworn Japanese-Spanish translation mandatory.
process.step4Desc: No time limit while the vehicle does not circulate. Restore to original specification (historic route) or repair and prepare for standard homologation.
process.step5Desc: Vehicles 30+ years in original condition: historic route (Reduced Technical Sheet). All others: individual homologation at INTA, INSIA or LCOE. Always check whether an equivalence code exists first.
process.step6Desc: Import ITV (individual) at an authorised station. Confirm beforehand that the station accepts this type of inspection.
process.step7Desc: Pay Registration Tax (form 576) and DGT fee (€99.77). Appointment at the Provincial Traffic Headquarters. Collect the Circulation Permit and request plates.

costs.sectionDesc: Each component of the total cost and what you need to know about each one.
costs.tariffText: The EU-Japan EPA Agreement (in force since 2019, phased in until 2026) reduces the tariff to 0% with correct origin documentation. Without it, the standard MFN rate of 10% applies. Always check the exact rate in TARIC code 8703 before each import.
costs.vatText: 21% on the CIF value (purchase price + freight + insurance) plus the tariff paid. In the Canary Islands, IGIC applies instead of VAT. Mandatory, no exceptions for commercial imports.
costs.homoText:
Historic (30+ years, original): €150–400, weeks.
Equivalence (existing code): €300–800, weeks.
Individual (laboratory): €1,500–2,000, 2–3 months.
Always consult an engineer before buying.
costs.matricText: Based on CO₂ emissions. From 0% (below 120 g/km) to 14.75% (above 200 g/km). Japanese sports cars from the 1990s with high-output engines typically fall in the 9.75%–14.75% band.
costs.translationText: Mandatory for customs, ITV and DGT. Sworn translation (Japanese → Spanish) by a translator accredited by the MAEC: €80–200. Hague Apostille in Japan: ¥1,000–3,000 per document. Turnaround: 5–7 working days.
costs.tipText: If the model was previously approved in Spain, an equivalence code may exist in the Ministry of Industry database. Asking an engineer to check before starting any procedure can save €1,000–1,500 and months of waiting.

faq.q1Title: Can I keep the car in the garage unregistered indefinitely?
faq.q1Text: Yes. There is no legal time limit for keeping an unregistered vehicle in a private garage as long as it does not use public roads. The obligation to register it only arises when you want to drive it.
faq.q2Title: Can I import a right-hand drive car?
faq.q2Text: Yes, for passenger cars without restriction. The ban on registering right-hand drive vehicles applies only to heavy goods vehicles (over 6 tonnes and 3.5 tonnes payload). Passenger cars, SUVs and JDM saloons can be registered with right-hand drive.
faq.q3Title: Does the car need to pass an ITV before entering Spain?
faq.q3Text: No. The vehicle can enter in a damaged or non-running condition. The registration ITV is carried out in Spain once the vehicle is repaired and homologated, before applying for the plate.
faq.q4Title: Is Japanese or foreign homologation valid in Spain?
faq.q4Text: No. Japan is not an EU member and its homologation system has no mutual recognition with Spain. All modification homologation must be obtained through the Spanish or European system. Japanese documentation serves as supporting technical evidence but does not replace the Spanish process.
faq.q5Title: What happens if the car fails the ITV?
faq.q5Text: You must correct the faults and re-present the vehicle within the following two months. If it is not re-inspected within that period, the registration process is cancelled and must be restarted from the ITV.

footer.text: Indicative tool updated in 2026. Real costs may vary depending on the vehicle condition, Hacienda valuation and regulatory changes. Always verify with a homologation engineer before buying.
